title: Done-for-you DOT compliance management for small/mid motor carriers
subindustry: Motor-carrier safety compliance administration (DQ files, Clearinghouse, filings)
product_service: Monthly per-driver/per-unit program: build and maintain driver qualification files (49 CFR 391.51), annual MVR pulls and reviews, medical-card expiry tracking, annual Clearinghouse limited queries (382.701), maintenance-file and annual-inspection tracking, MCS-150/UCR/IRP/IFTA filing calendar, new-entrant safety audit and compliance-review preparation, CSA score monitoring. Optional bundle with drug & alcohol consortium (WS17-002).
target_customer: Owners/office managers of motor carriers with 2-100 power units; Chicago 8-county area has 11,781 such carriers with MCS-150 updated 2024+ (5,288 with 6-100 PU) [A, WS17-S001]; also private fleets (construction 3,325 carriers, utility 824) [A, WS17-S001].
purchase_motivation: Legal mandate (DQ files, Clearinghouse queries, periodic inspections) with fines, failed new-entrant audits, insurance premium pressure from CSA scores, and shipper/broker vetting; small carriers lack staff to track dozens of expiring items.
spending_evidence: Mandate verified [A, WS17-S004, WS17-S005, WS17-S002]; buyer population verified [A, WS17-S001]. Actual outsourced-compliance spend per carrier NOT verified (MISSING) - web search budget exhausted before pricing could be gathered.
representative_operators: J. J. Keller & Associates - national compliance publisher/services provider (size not verified this session) [E]
Foley Services - driver screening/compliance services (not verified) [E]
Many local 'DOT compliance' consultants and insurance-agency-affiliated services (count unknown) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-driver per-month subscription plus one-time onboarding/file-rebuild and audit-prep fees; pass-through of MVR/state fees.
typical_transaction_value: Hypothesis: $25-$60 per driver per month; a 10-truck/12-driver carrier ~$300-$700/mo; audit-prep projects $500-$2,500 [E - unverified]
direct_costs: Compliance-coordinator labor, MVR and query pass-through fees, compliance software licences, E&O insurance.
contribution_profit_note: If one coordinator ($50-60k loaded, E) handles ~120-200 drivers with good tooling, contribution per coordinator ~$40-90k/yr at assumed prices [E].
working_capital_note: Bill monthly in advance by ACH/card; negligible inventory; receivables minimal if autopay enforced.
sales_cycle: 1-6 weeks for small carriers; faster when triggered by an audit letter, insurance renewal or new authority.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract - monthly; churn driven by carrier failure in freight downturns.
acquisition_channels: Direct mail/email to FMCSA census list (respect TCPA - no autodialed cell calls)
Truck insurance agents and factoring companies (referral partners)
New-authority filings (new entrants needing safety audits)
Ethnic trucking communities/associations in Chicago suburbs
customer_accessibility: High identifiability: every carrier's name, address, fleet size and often email/phone are in the public census [A, WS17-S001]. Winning trust is harder: carriers are bombarded with scam 'compliance' letters.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed in principle: MVRs, Clearinghouse and filing portals are open to carriers/agents; specific compliance software vendors not evaluated.
competitive_intensity: high - national publishers, telematics platforms adding DQ modules, insurance agencies offering free tools, and many low-cost consultants.
entry_strategy: Hyperlocal, multilingual, fully done-for-you service with an audit-ready guarantee and fixed monthly price; lead with free file audit; bundle consortium + filings; target 6-50 PU carriers too small for in-house safety staff.
licenses: No federal or Illinois licence identified for compliance administration [E - absence not verified]; must avoid legal advice (unauthorized practice of law). E&O insurance advisable. IFTA/IRP filings need carrier power of attorney.
regulatory_barriers: Low barrier to entry; risk of being lumped with deceptive 'FMCSA update' mailers - marketing must be scrupulously non-deceptive.
operational_risks: Missed expiry creates client fines and liability; data security of driver PII; dependence on timely client document submission.
financial_risks: High churn of small carriers during freight recessions (Rush reports freight recession pressure in 2025 [A, WS17-S021]); price competition.
geographic_constraints: Can be delivered remotely nationwide; Chicago gives dense local base.
founder_expertise: Learn FMCSRs Parts 382/391/395/396, filing systems, carrier operations; strong sales.
staffing: First compliance coordinator at ~40-60 clients; sales rep later; bilingual staff valuable.
automation_potential: High: document intake/OCR of med cards and MVRs, expiry tracking, automated reminders, audit-file assembly, CSA monitoring dashboards. Humans still handle client chasing, judgment calls and audits. Runs on ordinary SaaS + modest API costs.
delegation_potential: Good - coordinator roles are standard admin jobs with SOPs.
scalability: Remote delivery allows multi-state growth; ceiling limited by churn and price competition.
expansion: Consortium/C-TPA (WS17-002), IRP/IFTA and title services (WS17-031), maintenance tracking (WS17-009), insurance referral partnerships (WS02 cross-stream).
roic_note: Asset-light; <$15k at risk; returns depend on CAC and churn rather than capital.
critical_assumptions: Small carriers will pay $25-60/driver/month for outsourced compliance
unanswered_questions: Actual market prices of DOT compliance subscriptions in Chicago
Churn rates for small-carrier service contracts
How many of the 11,781 2-100 PU carriers already outsource compliance
failure_modes: Reputation damage from a client fined due to missed item
Founder becomes the only person who understands the rules
score_rationale: roic 8: <$15k capital. access 6: public census list but trust barrier. resilience 7: mandated, but buyers die in freight recessions. entry 4: crowded, weak wedge. ai 7: document-heavy workflow where tooling materially cuts labor per client.
preliminary_verdict: advance - mandated recurring demand, quantified local buyer base, asset-light; needs price/churn validation.

title: DOT drug & alcohol testing consortium / C-TPA for owner-operators and small fleets
subindustry: DOT consortium and third-party administrator services
product_service: Random-testing pool membership, pre-employment/post-accident/reasonable-suspicion test coordination via lab/MRO/collection-site network, Clearinghouse reporting on employer's behalf, annual MIS reports, supervisor training; optional DOT-qualified on-site collector.
target_customer: Owner-operators and fleets with CDL drivers; Chicago 8-county area has 17,611 recent-filing carriers with 1-5 power units [A, WS17-S001], plus construction/utility employers of CDL drivers.
purchase_motivation: Federal mandate: random testing at baseline 50% (drugs)/10% (alcohol) of driver positions [A, WS17-S006]; Clearinghouse queries [A, WS17-S005]; one-truck operators cannot randomize themselves alone.
spending_evidence: Mandate verified [A, WS17-S005, WS17-S006]; consortium pricing NOT verified (MISSING).
representative_operators: National online consortiums and C/TPAs (names/prices not verified this session) [E]
Occupational health clinics offering DOT testing [E]
revenue_mechanism: Annual enrollment fee per driver plus per-test fees with markup over lab/MRO/collection costs.
typical_transaction_value: Hypothesis: $75-$200 per driver per year enrollment plus $50-$90 markup-inclusive per drug test [E - unverified]
direct_costs: Lab fees, MRO review fees, third-party collection-site fees, software, staff time.
contribution_profit_note: Low per-member contribution (est. $50-$120/yr) - needs thousands of members or bundling [E].
working_capital_note: Annual fees collected upfront; lab invoices net 30 - slightly positive cash cycle.
sales_cycle: Days; triggered by new authority, new hire, or audit.
customer_accessibility: Owner-operators are numerous and identifiable, but the product is bought online on price.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: SAMHSA-certified labs, MROs and collection networks sell to C/TPAs; contract terms not verified.
entry_strategy: Do not compete standalone; offer as a bundled component of WS17-001 to raise retention and wallet share.
licenses: No specific Illinois licence identified [E]; must follow 49 CFR Part 40 procedures; collector training if collecting in-house [E].
regulatory_barriers: Procedural complexity (Part 40) and liability for errors; Clearinghouse reporting obligations.
operational_risks: Selection/notification errors invalidate random program; chain-of-custody mistakes.
staffing: One administrator can run a large pool with software.
automation_potential: Random selection, notifications, MIS reporting automated; collections stay physical.
expansion: Pre-employment screening, MVRs, background checks (WS12 cross-stream).
roic_note: Asset-light; profit limited by price competition.
critical_assumptions: Bundling raises retention of WS17-001 clients
unanswered_questions: Wholesale lab/MRO/collection rates available to a new C/TPA
score_rationale: resilience 8: hard federal mandate. entry 2: extreme price competition online. fcf 3: thin per-member contribution makes standalone profit small.
preliminary_verdict: hold - only as bundle component of WS17-001, not standalone.

title: Mobile fleet washing route (tractors, trailers, box trucks, vans, equipment) with wastewater capture
product_service: Scheduled on-site (often overnight) washing of tractors, trailers, straight trucks, delivery vans, buses and construction equipment, with reclaim mats/vacuum recovery; add-ons: aluminum brightening, undercarriage salt removal, degreasing, graffiti removal, decal-safe washing.
target_customer: Fleet/terminal managers at for-hire carriers (4,442 with 6-100 PU in the Chicago 8-county area [A, WS17-S001]), private fleets with branded trucks (food/beverage distribution, uniform, utilities), last-mile van operators, equipment owners, municipalities (bids).
purchase_motivation: Brand image for private fleets, road-salt corrosion control in Chicago winters, lighting/reflector visibility, customer requirements; avoids drivers' time at truck washes.
spending_evidence: No verified spend data gathered (MISSING). Fleet trailer base is large: 52,879 owned + 42,998 term-leased trailers among Chicago mid-size carriers [A, WS17-S001].
representative_operators: Fleet Clean USA - franchised mobile fleet washing (size/Item 19 not retrieved) [E]
Fleetwash - national fleet washing provider (not verified) [E]
Local independent operators (count unknown) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-unit wash price x frequency (weekly/biweekly/monthly) under standing schedules.
typical_transaction_value: Hypothesis: $25-$60 per tractor, $30-$75 per trailer, $15-$35 per van; a 40-unit customer washed biweekly ~$2,000-$4,000/mo [E - unverified]
direct_costs: Two-person crew labor (night work), water, detergents, fuel, equipment wear, wastewater recovery/disposal.
contribution_profit_note: A crew washing ~40-80 units/night at assumed prices could gross ~$1,500-$3,500/night; contribution after crew and supplies ~40-55% [E].
working_capital_note: Net-30 invoicing typical (assumed); minimal inventory.
sales_cycle: 2-8 weeks; trial wash then standing schedule.
acquisition_channels: Drive-by prospecting of truck yards (Elk Grove Village, Bensenville, Bolingbrook, Joliet)
customer_accessibility: Good - yards are visible and dense; decision maker is often the terminal or fleet manager.
supplier_accessibility: Confirmed in principle: pressure washers, reclaim systems and chemicals are widely sold (vendors not evaluated).
competitive_intensity: moderate-high - low skill barrier; incumbents include franchisees, independents, in-house wash bays and truck-stop washes.
entry_strategy: Be the documented-compliant operator (wastewater capture, insurance, background-checked crews) for brand-conscious private fleets and municipalities that must avoid illicit-discharge liability.
licenses: Business registration, insurance; wastewater: MS4 ordinances must prohibit non-stormwater discharge and commercial washing is not an allowable flow [A, WS17-S013]; MWRD/municipal sewer discharge approvals MISSING.
regulatory_barriers: Wash-water capture and disposal; possible local permits; chemical handling.
operational_risks: Chicago winter freezing limits outdoor washing for weeks; night labor turnover; damage claims.
financial_risks: Washing is among the first discretionary cuts in freight recessions.
founder_expertise: Equipment, chemistry, wastewater compliance, crew management.
staffing: Crews of 2 from day one if founder is not washing; crew lead per truck.
automation_potential: Route optimisation, scheduling, photo proof-of-service, invoicing; washing itself is manual.
delegation_potential: Moderate - standard labor roles, but turnover high.
scalability: Add rigs per ~15-30 customers; regional ceiling.
expansion: Pressure-washing of facilities, equipment detailing, decal removal for fleet remarketing (WS17-011).
roic_note: Rigs $15-60k each; payback plausibly <1 yr if routes fill [E].
critical_assumptions: Wastewater can be disposed lawfully at reasonable cost
unanswered_questions: MWRD and municipal rules for disposing mobile wash water
Fleet Clean USA FDD Item 19 data
score_rationale: resilience 4: discretionary in downturns and weather-exposed. feasibility 6: wastewater compliance adds real burden. entry 4: low skill barrier.
preliminary_verdict: hold - real recurring demand but low barriers, weather and discretionary spend; validate pricing first.

title: Mobile preventive maintenance for light/medium-duty service and delivery fleets
subindustry: On-site fleet PM (oil, brakes, inspections) for vans, pickups, box trucks
product_service: Scheduled on-site PM at customer yards (often overnight): oil/filters, multipoint and DVIR-defect repairs, brakes, batteries, wipers, tire rotation, recalls coordination, annual inspections for >10,001 lb units, digital maintenance records.
target_customer: Fleet owners/ops managers with 10-150 light/medium vehicles: last-mile delivery contractors, HVAC/plumbing/electrical/pest service companies, car-share/rental, private fleets; many vans are <10,001 lb and thus not in FMCSA data [A, WS17-S016].
purchase_motivation: Downtime: a van at a shop for a day loses a route; driver time savings; maintenance records for warranty/lease returns.
spending_evidence: Incumbents sell this: Ryder offers on-demand retail mobile maintenance (Torque by Ryder) and SelectCare maintenance ($680M 'SelectCare and other' revenue in 2025) [A, WS17-S022]; Rush runs mobile service units and on-site techs [A, WS17-S021]. Local spend MISSING.
representative_operators: Ryder (Torque by Ryder, SelectCare) - $680M SelectCare & other revenue 2025 [A, WS17-S022]
Rush Truck Centers mobile service [A, WS17-S021]
Venture-backed mobile fleet maintenance startups and local independents (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-service flat PM price plus labor-hour and parts markup on repairs; optional per-vehicle monthly plan.
typical_transaction_value: Hypothesis: $100-$200 per van PM; $300-$1,200 average repair ticket; 40-van customer ~$3,000-$8,000/mo [E]
direct_costs: Technician wages, parts (Rush parts GM 28-30% at incumbent scale [A, WS17-S021]), fluids, van/fuel, disposal of used oil.
contribution_profit_note: Labor-heavy mix lifts margin (incumbent service GM 66-68% [A, WS17-S021]) but new entrant loses efficiency to travel and no lifts; blended 35-55% assumed [E].
working_capital_note: Net-30 B2B; parts bought on account from local distributors; modest receivables.
sales_cycle: 2-8 weeks; trial on a few vehicles.
repeat_purchase: recurring-contract - PM every 5-10k miles / monthly visits.
acquisition_channels: Direct outreach to service-company fleets (visible branded vans)
Fleet management companies needing local vendors
customer_accessibility: Good - branded service fleets are visible and decision makers reachable; short cycles.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: local parts distributors (NAPA/GPC, others) sell to repair businesses on account.
competitive_intensity: high - dealers, quick lubes, independents, Ryder and startups.
entry_strategy: Yard-based night service with photo-documented PM and same-week DVIR defect repair; focus on 20-100 vehicle fleets too small for Ryder contracts.
licenses: No Illinois mechanic licence identified [E]; 625 ILCS 5/5-301 'repairers and rebuilders' licensing concerns rebuilt/salvage vehicles - confirm whether it captures general repair [A-statute heading, WS17-S011; applicability E]; used-oil handling rules; garage-keepers insurance.
regulatory_barriers: Low; environmental handling of fluids on customer sites.
operational_risks: Technician hiring/retention; work limited without lifts; weather.
founder_expertise: Must learn fleet maintenance basics and hire competent techs; sales focus.
staffing: First automotive tech before or at launch (founder lacks mechanical skills); service writer/dispatcher by ~3 techs.
automation_potential: Scheduling, route planning, parts lookup, estimate writing, maintenance-record reports, telematics-triggered PM; wrench time remains human.
delegation_potential: Moderate - standard tech roles but shortage-prone labor market (Rush cites technician retention as competitive factor [A, WS17-S021]).
scalability: Add service vans per ~150-300 vehicles under care; regional.
expansion: Medium-duty/box trucks, trailer repair (WS17-006), fleet maintenance management (WS17-009), EV light-van service.
roic_note: ~$40-70k per equipped service van; plausible 1-2 yr payback per van at full utilization [E].
critical_assumptions: Techs can be hired at workable wages
Fleets accept on-site PM pricing above quick-lube
unanswered_questions: Chicago automotive/diesel tech wages (BLS OEWS not retrievable this session)
Count of 10-150 vehicle service fleets in Chicago (no public register for <10,001 lb vans)
failure_modes: Founder unable to supervise quality without mechanical knowledge
score_rationale: resilience 7: maintenance non-discretionary. entry 5: service/speed wedge, easily copied. delegation 5: dependent on scarce techs.
preliminary_verdict: advance - recurring non-discretionary demand with incumbent validation; technician supply is the key risk to test.

title: Mobile heavy-duty diesel repair and roadside service (Class 6-8)
subindustry: Mobile truck/diesel repair and roadside breakdown service
product_service: Roadside and yard repairs for tractors and heavy trucks: diagnostics, air/brake, electrical, cooling, aftertreatment sensors, jump/fuel, minor engine work; PM at yards.
target_customer: Carriers with Class 7-8 tractors (47,221 owned tractors among Chicago mid-size carriers [A, WS17-S001]), owner-operators, breakdown-management networks, brokers.
purchase_motivation: Downtime cost and load deadlines; towing alternative is expensive.
spending_evidence: Rush operates mobile service units/techs at customer sites [A, WS17-S021]. Local price data MISSING.
representative_operators: Rush Truck Centers mobile service [A, WS17-S021]
Dealer and independent mobile diesel operators (unquantified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Hourly labor plus call-out fee and parts markup; after-hours premiums.
typical_transaction_value: Hypothesis: $150-$200/hr labor, $500-$2,500 per roadside ticket [E - unverified]
direct_costs: Diesel tech wages, parts, service truck (crane, compressor, welder), fuel, insurance.
contribution_profit_note: One utilised truck+tech could produce $150-$300k revenue/yr at assumed rates; contribution 40-55% [E].
working_capital_note: Roadside often paid by card/comchek at service; fleet accounts net 30.
sales_cycle: Immediate for roadside (buyers search actively); weeks for fleet accounts.
repeat_purchase: occasional - roadside; recurring for fleet PM accounts.
customer_accessibility: Roadside buyers actively search; fleet accounts via outreach.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: HD parts distributors sell on account.
competitive_intensity: high - dealers and many independent operators.
entry_strategy: Guaranteed response-time zones along I-55/I-80/I-294 logistics corridors; night coverage.
licenses: No IL mechanic licence identified [E]; commercial auto + garage liability insurance; used fluid handling.
operational_risks: Diesel technician scarcity; safety on roadside; complex jobs require shop.
financial_risks: Expensive service truck; freight cycle reduces repair spend at margin.
founder_expertise: Founder cannot do the work; must hire experienced diesel techs and learn dispatch/pricing.
staffing: Diesel tech(s) at launch; dispatcher later.
automation_potential: Dispatch, diagnostics lookups, quoting, invoicing; repairs manual.
delegation_potential: Moderate-low - quality depends on scarce senior techs.
roic_note: $60-150k per truck; returns hinge on utilisation [E].
critical_assumptions: Experienced diesel techs can be hired
unanswered_questions: Diesel tech wage levels in Chicago (BLS not retrieved)
Utilisation achievable by a new entrant
score_rationale: access 7: roadside buyers search actively. delegation 4: depends on scarce senior diesel techs and founder lacks the trade. resilience 6: repairs needed but freight cyclical.
preliminary_verdict: hold - real demand, but tech-constrained and founder cannot perform or supervise the trade initially.

title: Mobile trailer repair and trailer PM (dry van/reefer box, lights, air, doors, floors, welding)
product_service: Yard-based trailer service: lighting/electrical, air lines and gladhands, drum brakes/slack adjusters, ABS, mudflaps, roll-up and swing doors, side panels, floors, landing gear, welding, reflective tape; trailer PM programs and inspection-readiness checks.
target_customer: Carriers with trailer pools (52,879 owned + 42,998 term-leased trailers among 5,288 Chicago-area carriers with 6-100 PU [A, WS17-S001]); warehouses/DCs with drop-trailer yards; trailer lessors.
purchase_motivation: Every trailer must pass periodic inspection and be maintained to Appendix A standards [A, WS17-S002]; out-of-service violations; damaged doors/lights stop loads.
spending_evidence: Mandate verified [A, WS17-S002]; large local trailer base [A, WS17-S001]; price data MISSING.
representative_operators: Trailer dealers' service departments and independent mobile trailer repair operators (not verified) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Hourly labor + parts markup; per-trailer PM flat fee; yard service days.
typical_transaction_value: Hypothesis: $100-$150/hr; $150-$800 per trailer repair; yard day $1,500-$3,000 [E]
direct_costs: Trailer tech wages, parts, service truck, welding consumables.
contribution_profit_note: Trailer work is parts-light and labor-heavy; contribution ~45-55% assumed [E].
working_capital_note: Net-30 fleet invoicing assumed; small parts inventory on truck.
acquisition_channels: Yard canvassing in O'Hare/Elk Grove/Bensenville and I-55/I-80 corridors
customer_accessibility: Good - trailer-heavy carriers identifiable from census trailer counts [A, WS17-S001]; yards dense.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: trailer parts distributors sell on account.
competitive_intensity: moderate - fragmented independents; dealers focus on shops.
entry_strategy: Trailer-only specialization (lower skill barrier than engine work; techs trainable faster) with scheduled yard days and photo reports.
licenses: No IL licence identified [E]. NOTE: Illinois runs its own periodic safety-test program at Official Testing Stations, with inspections performed inside the OTS building [A, WS17-S007, WS17-S008] - mobile federal annual inspections may not satisfy Illinois requirements for IL-based trailers; verify before selling inspections.
regulatory_barriers: Low for repair; Illinois inspection regime limits a mobile 'annual inspection' revenue line.
operational_risks: Welding/fire safety in yards; tech retention; winter work.
geographic_constraints: Route density; Chicago is a strong trailer market.
founder_expertise: Learn trailer systems; hire one experienced trailer tech; sell.
staffing: One trailer tech at launch; helpers trainable.
delegation_potential: Moderate-good - trailer techs easier to train than diesel engine techs [E].
scalability: Add trucks; regional; adjacency to OTS shop.
expansion: OTS station (WS17-008), liftgate repair (WS17-024), chassis M&R (WS17-007), trailer leasing (WS17-028).
unanswered_questions: Whether IL-registered trailers require IDOT OTS testing (thresholds)
Share of carriers with in-house trailer techs
score_rationale: access 7: trailer-heavy carriers identifiable and dense. delegation 6: trailer work more trainable than engine work. resilience 6: maintenance needed but freight-cyclical.
preliminary_verdict: advance - large verified local trailer base and lower skill barrier than diesel engine work.

spending_evidence: Mandate verified [A, WS17-S002]; contract values MISSING.
representative_operators: Established M&R vendors at terminals (not verified this session) [E]
revenue_mechanism: Per-repair tariff or hourly contracts; sometimes dedicated crews.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING - contract M&R tariffs not retrieved [E]
direct_costs: Mechanic crews, parts, tires, yard trucks, insurance.
contribution_profit_note: Volume-driven, tariff-constrained margins [E].
working_capital_note: Net 45-60 typical for large IEPs [E]; payroll weekly - cash gap.
sales_cycle: 3-12 months; vendor qualification, insurance, safety programs.
customer_accessibility: Low-moderate - concentrated buyers with procurement walls and incumbent vendors.
competitive_intensity: moderate - few qualified vendors per terminal but entrenched.
entry_strategy: Start as subcontractor or serve drayage carriers' own chassis; build safety record.

title: Illinois Official Testing Station (public truck/trailer safety lane) with repair upsell
subindustry: State-mandated commercial vehicle safety testing (IDOT OTS) and diesel emissions testing
product_service: IDOT-permitted public Official Testing Station performing periodic safety tests for trucks, trailers, buses and rebuilt vehicles (semiannual for Illinois Vehicle Code vehicles, annual for interstate units per VIR categories), issuing Certificates of Safety; repair of failed items in an attached bay; possible diesel emissions testing for intrastate diesel >16,000 lb in Chicago-area counties.
target_customer: Illinois-based carriers and private fleets of second-division vehicles; ~25,049 recent-filing carriers in the 8-county area [A, WS17-S001]; intrastate carriers (981 with 2+ PU) subject to semiannual tests and diesel emissions testing [A, WS17-S001, WS17-S007].
purchase_motivation: State mandate - no valid safety test, no lawful operation; failures must be repaired and retested.
spending_evidence: Mandate and station network (~250-260 OTS statewide) verified [A, WS17-S007]; per-test prices charged by stations NOT found (MISSING).
representative_operators: ~260 Illinois OTS performing truck/trailer/rebuilt inspections, often truck repair shops and dealers [A, WS17-S007]
revenue_mechanism: Per-test fee (market-set) plus repair labor/parts on failed items and retests.
typical_transaction_value: MISSING - test fees not published; hypothesis $40-$100 per test plus repair upsell [E]
direct_costs: Certified Safety Tester wages, building lease (bay sized for tractor-trailer), equipment, bond, insurance, IDOT fees.
contribution_profit_note: Highly dependent on test volume per lane-day and repair attach rate (both MISSING) [E].
working_capital_note: Paid at time of test (cash/card) - favourable; repair parts small.
sales_cycle: Walk-in/scheduled; fleets choose stations by location and turnaround.
customer_accessibility: High - every Illinois commercial vehicle must test; convenience-driven choice.
supplier_accessibility: Permit process is public: written application to IDOT, $1,000 bond, at least one CST, location-specific permit, building dimension rules for new OTS from July 2025 [A, WS17-S008].
competitive_intensity: moderate - ~260 stations statewide; local density unknown.
entry_strategy: Fast-turnaround lane in an underserved corridor with appointment booking and same-day repair of failures.
licenses: IDOT OTS permit (Public), $1,000 surety bond, at least one Certified Safety Tester employee, applicant 18+, application fee ($10 in Cornell copy; ~$50 per current ILGA text via search summary) [A, WS17-S008]. CST certification requirements MISSING.
regulatory_barriers: Building requirements and permit; IDOT audits; permanent denial after serious violations [A, WS17-S008].
operational_risks: Integrity risk (pressure to pass vehicles) - fraud would end the business; tester availability.
financial_risks: Lease of a large bay is a fixed cost before volume arrives.
founder_expertise: IDOT rules, shop operations; hire CST.
staffing: CST from day one; mechanic for repairs.
automation_potential: Booking, VIR paperwork, reminders to fleets when tests expire (strong retention lever).
delegation_potential: Good - CST employees run lanes under SOPs.
scalability: Limited per site; multi-site possible but permit/building per site.
expansion: Trailer/truck repair shop (WS17-034), diesel emissions, DOT compliance (WS17-001).
roic_note: Moderate capital (bay lease, equipment); mandated recurring flows; real returns unknown without test-fee data.
critical_assumptions: Test fees and volumes support a dedicated lane
CST can be hired or trained
unanswered_questions: Whether IL-based interstate units must test at OTS or can use 396.17 inspections
failure_modes: Integrity violation leading to permit loss
Being out-competed by repair shops that use OTS as a feeder
score_rationale: resilience 8: state-mandated periodic tests. cash 9: paid at service. scale 4: site-bound. feasibility 6: permit, bond, building, CST.

title: Outsourced fleet maintenance management for 15-300 vehicle service fleets
product_service: Per-vehicle-per-month program: PM scheduling from mileage/telematics, a vetted vendor network (shops, mobile techs, tire, glass, body), repair-estimate approval against labor-time guides, invoice audit, consolidated billing, recall tracking, DQ/inspection tracking for >10,001 lb units, replacement-cycle analytics.
target_customer: Owners/COOs/office managers of companies with 15-300 vehicles and no dedicated fleet manager: HVAC/plumbing/electrical contractors, landscapers, pest control, home health, utility and telecom contractors, construction (3,325 Chicago-area carriers flag construction cargo [A, WS17-S001]).

Large fleet management companies (Holman, Element, Wheels - not verified this session) [E]

direct_costs: Fleet coordinator labor, software, vendor onboarding, credit risk if consolidated billing.
contribution_profit_note: One coordinator could manage ~400-800 vehicles with tooling [E].
working_capital_note: If consolidated billing, the firm pays vendors before collecting from clients - working capital and credit risk; avoid initially by having vendors bill clients directly.
sales_cycle: 1-3 months; ROI-driven sale with savings audit.
customer_accessibility: Moderate - SMB fleets numerous but unregistered below 10,001 lb; branded vans identifiable on the street.
supplier_accessibility: Assumed: independent shops welcome volume referrals; terms to be negotiated.
competitive_intensity: moderate - large FMCs target bigger fleets; SMB segment served by telematics software (self-serve) rather than done-for-you.
entry_strategy: Guaranteed-savings audit for 15-300 vehicle fleets ignored by large FMCs; disclosed pricing (no hidden markups) as trust wedge.
licenses: None identified [E].
regulatory_barriers: Low; transparency on vendor rebates to avoid conflicts.
financial_risks: Credit risk if paying vendors on clients' behalf.

automation_potential: High: estimate review vs labor guides, invoice audit, telematics-triggered PM, vendor scoring, reporting.

expansion: Own mobile PM crews (WS17-004), remarketing (WS17-011), compliance (WS17-001).
